workstream: U34 -- CaraResidualEnv: a separate residual-RL environment retaining the complete teacher at 500Hz, learned corrections at 50Hz. Integration milestone only -- NO PPO training this session.

architecture.teacher_500hz: gait.py's ENTIRE control law (unmodified source) -- phase state machine, swing tables, U9 lateral-roll balance trim -- recomputes from the CURRENT live simulator state every physics substep (2ms), exactly as it always has. Nothing extracted or re-derived (per instruction: extracting only the balance loop would introduce another untested controller).
architecture.policy_50hz: requests a bounded correction dq_RL, held constant for 10 physics substeps (matching CaraWalkEnv's own substeps=10). The residual bound applies to dq_RL ONLY -- the combined command is never re-clipped to CaraWalkEnv's nominal-centered [-1,1] bound, which would recreate U32/U33's demonstrated failure.
architecture.final_limits: joint limits only (mirrors gait.py's own behavior, which never self-clips beyond the model's physical range). Actuator FORCE limits are already enforced by MuJoCo's <position> servo + forcerange, unaffected.
architecture.mechanism: gait.py's run()/walk() are deeply nested closures with no external pause hook. Implemented via a background thread running gait.py's own run() call, synchronized with the main thread at every mujoco.mj_step() call through a producer/consumer queue pair -- the same non-invasive monkeypatch technique as U32/U33, extended to hold ONLY the residual (not the full combined signal) between decision points so the teacher's own 500Hz reactivity is preserved between policy decisions.

bug_found_and_fixed_before_trusting_anyt.description: An earlier version held the FULL combined (teacher+residual) signal constant for all 10 substeps between decisions -- silently degrading the TEACHER itself to 50Hz too, discarding its intended 500Hz reactivity between policy decisions.
bug_found_and_fixed_before_trusting_anyt.how_caught: The zero-residual equivalence check (milestone 1, run BEFORE trusting the architecture) reproduced U33's 50Hz/native FAILURE (fell at decision step 303, tilt 42.0deg) instead of U33's 500Hz/native SUCCESS -- an unambiguous signal given U33's own numbers were already on record.
bug_found_and_fixed_before_trusting_anyt.fix: Only the residual (combined_target_at_decision - raw_teacher_target_at_decision) is held between decisions; the teacher's own contribution is re-read from data.ctrl (which gait.py freshly rewrites) on every intermediate substep and re-summed with the held residual before each physics step.

milestone_1_zero_residual_equivalence.requirement: Match the full 47.3s trial -- actual steps, progress, stopping, peak tilt -- not just survival. Reset all teacher state correctly.
milestone_1_zero_residual_equivalence.method: Fresh background thread (fresh gait.run() call, fresh model/data) started on every reset() -- no state leakage between episodes by construction.

result_after_fix.survived: 2365/2365 decisions (all of it), matching U33's 500Hz/native reference exactly on survival
result_after_fix.gait_own_report: gait.py's own printed output (a side effect of the background thread's call) shows the IDENTICAL result to its native run: step1 l_ PASS, step2 r_ PASS, 57mm total advance (31,27mm), MILESTONE MET.
result_after_fix.measurement_resolution_caveat: U34 samples tilt once per 50Hz decision (every 10th substep); U33's 500Hz condition sampled every substep. A true peak between U34's sample points could be missed -- the near-identical values (4.39 vs 4.3915) suggest this doesn't matter here (the reference trial has no violent transient), but it's a real resolution difference, disclosed rather than assumed negligible.

full_trajectory_bitexact_check.requirement: identical final distance and printed metrics establish excellent agreement, but full bit-for-bit trajectory equivalence requires comparing the state/control traces.
full_trajectory_bitexact_check.method: Recorded the full 19-dim qpos vector at every decision boundary for (a) U34's zero-residual replay, and (b) a genuinely independent pure gait.py run (same monkeypatch technique, no CaraResidualEnv involved at all) over the SAME 2-step walk.
full_trajectory_bitexact_check.conclusion: Genuinely bit-for-bit identical across the ENTIRE trajectory, not just final/summary metrics -- the strongest form of the equivalence claim, now verified rather than inferred from matching endpoints.

milestone_2_residual_bound_probes.requirement: Start with a few physically interpretable corrections and measure their effect. Choose correction bounds from these probes, rather than copying action_range_frac=0.30.
milestone_2_residual_bound_probes.method: cara_description/scripts/probe_residual_bound.py -- a CONSTANT residual (same value every decision, for the WHOLE episode) applied to one joint pair at a time (ankle_roll, hip_roll), at several magnitudes and both signs, on top of the otherwise-unmodified teacher.
milestone_2_residual_bound_probes.finding: Results were ASYMMETRIC and mostly fragile, not a clean symmetric safe zone: for ankle_roll, +0.003 to +0.005 rad survived cleanly (peak tilt slightly BETTER than the zero-residual reference: 3.77-3.99deg vs 4.39deg), but the NEGATIVE direction failed at EVERY tested magnitude from -0.001 rad up to -0.05 rad. hip_roll showed the same pattern (+0.005 survived with a small tilt cost, -0.005 failed immediately).
milestone_2_residual_bound_probes.interpretation: A temporally-CONSTANT bias inevitably opposes the teacher's own alternating balance correction (U9's trim sign depends on which foot is currently stance, flipping every step) during roughly half the gait cycle -- this probe measures a WORST CASE (a residual with the wrong sign for the current phase), not what a phase-aware learned policy would actually do. It does not, by itself, identify a bidirectional safe magnitude; it establishes an upper bound on how large a phase-naive constant offset can be before it becomes unsafe in its worse-case sign.
milestone_2_residual_bound_probes.SUPERSEDED: This constant-bias probe and its 0.005 rad conclusion are SUPERSEDED by the phase-indexed pulse probe below (U35 prep), which isolates the confound this probe left open (per external review: joint-sign convention, which leg, and the phase when the bias began were never separated from 'opposes the alternating trim'). Kept here for the record, not as the operative bound.

milestone_2b_phase_indexed_pulse_probes.requirement: Use brief, phase-indexed residual pulses instead of another constant-bias sweep: test each ankle-roll channel separately, apply equal +/- pulses at the CORRESPONDING left/right support phase, return smoothly to zero, record immediate response/later touchdown/completion.
milestone_2b_phase_indexed_pulse_probes.method: cara_description/scripts/probe_phase_pulse.py -- for each ankle-roll channel, tested at the decision window where THAT foot is actually the stance/trimmed foot per gait.py's own convention (a_roll = stance_leg + 'ankle_roll': r_ankle_roll during step 0 [lead=l_], l_ankle_roll during step 1 [lead=r_]). A smoothstep-on / hold / smoothstep-off pulse (20 decisions on, ramps 10 decisions each side, ~0.6s total) at several magnitudes, both signs, teacher targets and actuator limits unchanged.
milestone_2b_phase_indexed_pulse_probes.bug_found_and_fixed_before_trusting_resu: CaraResidualEnv.step() clips the incoming residual to cfg.residual_bound_rad, which DEFAULTS TO 0.02. The first probe run never overrode this, so every requested magnitude above 0.02 (0.05, 0.1, 0.15) was silently clipped down to 0.02 before reaching the physics -- caught because results across those magnitudes were suspiciously near-identical/saturated instead of monotonically varying. Fixed by having the probe construct its own CaraResidualEnvConfig with a bound wide enough for whatever magnitude is under test.
milestone_2b_phase_indexed_pulse_probes.finding: Completely different picture from the constant-bias sweep: SYMMETRIC and predictable. Both l_ankle_roll and r_ankle_roll survive cleanly, in BOTH signs, up to +/-0.05 rad (peak tilt barely moves: 4.39-4.48deg vs the 4.39deg reference), then fail in both signs somewhere between 0.05 and 0.1 rad (0.1/0.15 rad pulses cause real falls, tilt 38-43deg). This directly confirms the reviewer's point: the earlier asymmetry was a whole-episode confound (a constant bias fighting the alternating trim for half the walk), not a fundamental sign-sensitivity of these joints or this architecture. A brief, phase-localized pulse behaves symmetrically.
milestone_2b_phase_indexed_pulse_probes.chosen_default: residual_bound_rad = 0.05 (radians) -- REPLACES the earlier 0.005 rad figure, a full order of magnitude more generous, now supported by a methodologically sound (phase-matched, symmetric, brief-pulse) test rather than a confounded one. Tested one joint at a time; simultaneous multi-joint residuals (as a real policy would produce) were not tested here -- disclosed, not assumed to compose safely.

milestone_3_controller_context_exposed.requirement: Include gait phase/support mode, current teacher targets, and previous applied residual, alongside proprioception. Document any teacher inputs that currently require privileged simulator state.

observation_vector_65d.proprioception_30d: 12 joint positions + 12 joint velocities + 3 projected-gravity components + 3 base angular velocity components -- all available via ordinary IMU + joint encoders on real hardware, not privileged.
observation_vector_65d.controller_context_10d: 8-way one-hot gait phase (settle/A/B/C/D/E/final_hold/done) + 2 foot-contact booleans (support mode) -- phase computed via EXACT arithmetic on the physics-substep counter against gait.py's own scripted phase durations (settle=750, ramp=2000, swing=2000, etc. substeps, all read from the YAML config, cross-checked once against U33's own recorded total of 23650 substeps for n_steps=2) -- not extracted from gait.py's internals, since it exposes no hook for this. Support mode from ACTUAL simulated foot-floor contact, an honestly observable (not scripted) quantity.
observation_vector_65d.teacher_and_residual_24d: 12 current teacher target values (radians, offset from nominal) + 12 previous applied residual values.
observation_vector_65d.command_1d: desired_vx (fixed per-episode for this integration milestone).

milestone_3_controller_context_exposed.privileged_state_disclosure: gait.py's OWN control law (unchanged, per instruction) reads data.subtree_com -- the exact rigid-body center of mass -- every substep for its lateral balance trim. This is genuinely privileged: real hardware would need a full CAD mass model plus forward kinematics (or a dynamic estimator) to approximate it, not a direct sensor reading. Swing-foot height and stance-foot position (data.geom_xpos) are approximable via forward kinematics from joint encoders. Base orientation (qpos[3:7]) is an ordinary IMU-equivalent quantity. This dependency belongs to the TEACHER, which per instruction is retained unchanged -- it does not appear directly in the POLICY's own observation vector above, but the teacher's resulting targets (which the policy does see) are downstream of it.

milestone_4_reward_accounting_at_50hz.requirement: The teacher's ten internal updates must not multiply the alive reward. Separate penalties on residual changes from measurements of total commanded motion.
milestone_4_reward_accounting_at_50hz.implementation: Reward computed exactly ONCE per env.step() call (i.e. once per 10 physics substeps / once per 50Hz decision), using the state AFTER those 10 substeps complete -- structurally cannot be multiplied by the teacher's internal update count, since the teacher's substep-level activity is entirely inside the background thread and never triggers a separate reward evaluation.
milestone_4_reward_accounting_at_50hz.components: alive (+1/step), vel (tracking desired_vx), upright (sign-corrected v4 formula, same as CaraWalkEnv), effort (on the COMBINED command's fractional deviation from nominal -- a measurement of TOTAL commanded motion, logged and weighted), residual_rate (on the RESIDUAL's own step-to-step change ONLY, normalized by residual_bound_rad -- kept SEPARATE from the effort/total-motion term, per instruction). info['total_commanded_motion'] also exposed directly as an unweighted measurement.

hardware_dependency_recorded: Retaining 500Hz feedback in simulation does not establish that eventual sensors and servos can support a 500Hz control loop. Recorded here for actuator/controller selection: if this architecture is carried toward hardware, the TEACHER's control rate (not just the RL policy's 50Hz) is a real hardware requirement to validate separately.
frozen_comparison_preserved: cara_env.py / CaraWalkEnv is completely untouched -- this is a NEW, separate module (cara_residual_env.py). Regression-checked after this work: CaraWalkEnv's zero-action self-test and reward_audit.py both still pass unchanged.
not_done_this_turn: No PPO training, no behavior cloning, no comparison of teacher-only vs teacher+residual under a disturbance family (that is explicitly RL's first objective, gated on this integration milestone, which is what was delivered here). No U31 actor reuse (correctly not done -- its actions have a different meaning, as instructed). Residual actor's mean initialization at zero is a design note for the not-yet-built training script, not implemented here since no actor exists yet.
